To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

game modding is a socio-technical phenomenon in which the affordances that modders encounter and use shape the modding process, the modders' careers, and the modders' relationships with game companies.
modding affordances can serve to organize the mod scene and modding practices, but that the affordances can also constrain what can be modded, how mods can be made, and what can be done with mods.

computer game mods are developed by modders in mod teams, and modders are organized by a set of socio-technical and social affordances that shape their practices and interactions with other modders and the industry.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the social and technical conditions that make possible the emergence of a modding scene.
understanding the social, technical and legal factors that influence how game mods are developed, shared, and consumed.
how the affordances that are associated with game mods serve to organize and shape the modding scene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
modding is a complex, dynamic socio-technical phenomenon.
game mods, modders, modding, and the mod scene are a socio-technical accomplishment that depends on a wide range of associated affordances.
modders have been able to exploit a range of affordances to make game modding a vibrant and successful activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mod scene is a socio-technical phenomenon that emerges from the intersection of a variety of affordances that are both internal to the games themselves, as well as external to them, including the modders' career contingencies, the organizational practices of mod development teams, the social worlds intersecting with the mod scene, and the game industry itself.

the mod scene is a complex socio-technical ecology, where different kinds of affordances are used to shape and constrain the actions of the modders, and the mod scene is in turn used by the industry as an experimental ground for innovation.
the modding scene is an important site for understanding the socio-technical organization of computer game innovation and the emergence of new practices of computer game development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mod scene is not just a matter of a few individuals tinkering with game software.

the mod scene can be seen as a complex socio-technical system, and as such, the mod scene is not simply a product of the affordances that modders encounter, nor is it simply a reflection of the modders' own actions.

modding practices and the mod scene cannot be fully understood in the terms of the affordances that they are built upon, but must instead be understood in terms of the affordance networks that modders and the games industry have built together.
